capabilities: Opens .csv and .tsv files in a dedicated table view
Filters visible rows by searching across cells
Switches between table and source views with line numbers
Detects comma, semicolon, and pipe delimiters and parses quoted or multiline fields
Reports parse warnings, uneven row lengths, BOMs, and large-file render caps
extras: Renders only the first 10,000 rows of large files and reports the rest as a count; makes no network requests and never writes back to data files.
motivation: The author made it read-only because CSV editing is error-prone: quotes, escaped quotes, multiline cells, delimiters, and line endings can all be damaged by a casual edit flow, so v0.1 never writes to disk.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to inspect CSV or TSV data files as tables; they open as raw text, so checking exports, logs, or datasets means leaving the vault.

relations.evidence: Parses quoted fields, escaped quotes, and multiline fields with Papa Parse.

summary: Read-only viewer that opens .csv and .tsv files as searchable tables with a source view and parse warnings.
